2. The facts leading to the issuance of the Rule in a nutshell can be stated thus, the present opposite party no.1 being pre-emptor filed the original miscellaneous case in the court of learned Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar, Jhenaidah contending inter alia that the pre-emptor is a house wife and residing in Dhaka with her husband. Coming to her father's residence situated at Jhenidah the pre-emptor came to learn on 09.02.1997 that the opposite party no. 2 transferred the case land measuring 2½  decimals in favour of the opposite party no.1 on 30.01.1995 A.D. The pre-emptor-opposite party no.1 is a co-sharer by purchase the case joie after purchasing the land appertaining to S.A. Khatian No. 140/1 in plot no, 190 measuring an area of .05 acres of land from the original owner of the land opposite party no. 2 Rejia Khatun and for that reason for getting the land pre-empted due to her necessity after obtaining the certified copy of the case kabla on 15.03.1997 A.D. filed the original case for pre-emption under section 96 of the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950. The further case of the pre-emptor-opposite party no.1 is such that she has no other land excepting her purchased 05 decimals of land. 

 9. The learned Advocate also submits that the positive case of the purchaser-pre-emptee-petitioner that after his purchase in the year 1996 there was a survey of the land in presence of the pre-emptor's father. The witness no. 3 of the pre-emptor Md. Ammd Hossain, who is the father of the pre-emptor & the pre-emptor banks upon whom is a lawyer of the court. This important witness not challenged or denied the aforesaid proposition of the pre-emptee in his deposition. Therefore, the very circumstances go to show that the conduct of the witness no. 3 is amounting to admission of the pre-emptee's case. Apart from this; it was another contention of the pre-emptee that a "salish" was held in the month of February, 1996 and in that "salish" many witnesses were present, but none of them was produced from the side of the pre-emptor to establish her case to discard the assertion of the pre-emptee. On the other hand among the witnesses of the pre-emptees the witness no. 3, who is the husband of the vendor-opposite party no. 2 corroborate the case of the pre-emptee-petitioner including the above mentioned Salish. The witness no. 4 for the pre-emptee in his deposition specifically asserts that in the month of March 1996 the service of notice was done in presence of the father of the pre-emptor. This witness no. 4 is one of the co-sharer of the case jote and his statement is not denied or challenged even from the side of the pre-emptor during cross-examination. No denial even is noticed from the side of the pre-emptor. Among the four witnesses from the side of the pre-emptee-appellant-petitioner none of the witnesses was discussed or evaluated or even considered by the trial court as well as the appellate court and the very act of the learned courts below makes it clear that there has been total non-consideration of material evidence from the side of both the courts. Accordingly, the findings and observation is one-sided which is perverse in the eye of law and not sustainable. The learned counsel on behalf of the present petitioner lastly submits that the case is bad for defect of parties as the witness no. 4 for the pre-emptee Abdur Razzak and one Dr. Abdul Malek are the necessary parties in the instant case which is transpired from the cross-examination of the witness no.1 for the pre-emptor-opposite party as the pre-emptor not denied it. In absence of the aforesaid persons it cannot be held that the case is not bad for defect of parties but the courts below arbitrarily held that there is no such defect in the instant case for which the case may fail. It is on record that on 01.06.1998 A.D. the pre-emptor cited three persons as her witnesses, who are the Advocates of the local bar but during trial none of them was examined from her side and there is no explanation as to why those important witnesses were withheld and in this context under section 114(g) of the Evidence Act the presumptive value is such that had they been examined that would not have supported the pre-emptor's case. 

 14. We have come across from the deposition of the witnesses that the pre-emptor in her deposition regarding her date of knowledge states at a stage, “গত ০৬-০২-১৯৯৮ ইং তারিখের পূর্বে আমি নাঃ কবালার বিষয় জানতাম না” In her cross-examination she states in the very beginning that in the month of February, 1994 she went into possession of her land measuring .05 acres and for that portion of land she has mutated her name and she paid rent separately and independently for her portion of land. The witness no. 2 for the pre-emptor being an official of land office, Jhenidah Sadar, brought a mutation case record being No. 51/9-1/95-96. The last witness Md. Amzad Hossein, who is the father of the pre-emptor in his testimony states at a stage that the pre-emptee constructed wall in his land including the case land after his purchase. He also admits that the purchaser of the case land is a co-sharer by purchase in the case jote. He contradicted his daughter regarding mutation of the purchased land of his daughter (P.W.1) and payment of rent separately. On the other hand; the witness no.1 for the pre-emptee is the pre-emptee himself Md. Ismail Hossain, who corroborate his pleading as mentioned in his written objection. The witness no. 2 for the pre-emptee Md. Abdul Motaleb is a deed-writer of Jhenidah Sadar Sub-registry office and as such he is a formal witness of the case. The witness no. 3 Md. Abdul Aziz Mallick is the husband of vendor-opposite party no. 2. This witness asserts in his deposition that he himself told the father of the pre-emptor to purchase the case land prior to the pre-emptee-opposite party no. 1. The last witness Md. Abdur Razzak is a co-sharer of the case jote who states in his deposition that there was a survey in respect of the case land in the month of February, 1996 and at that time the pre-emptor's father was present 

 15. Consulting the relevant evidence it is evident to note that in respect of the alleged date of knowledge of the pre-emptor in the instant case no such independent, disinterested credible evidence is transpired by which it can be held that the pre-emptor in fact was in the dark about the disputed transfer which was in the year 1995. The witnesses who deposed in favour of the pre-emptor's case are not trustworthy and they obviously contradicted one-another in respect of the positive case of the pre-emptor. Specially; the pre-emptor and her father states contradictory statement before the trial court at the time of giving their deposition which has completely left out from the notice of both the courts below.
